confirmed.statement: S1-S4: The paper explicitly states that condition assignments were random in all experiments and administered by Qualtrics.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, Materials and Methods, final paragraph.

confirmed.statement: S1: Individual participants were randomly assigned between subjects to Perplexity AI assistance or their own judgment with optional search-engine use while listing playoff teams.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 12, Materials and Methods, Experiment 1, second paragraph.

confirmed.statement: S2: Individual participants were randomly assigned between subjects to Google Bard assistance or a no-LLM condition using their judgment and a browser or search engine; a Google account was required.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 13, Materials and Methods, Experiment 2; p. 5, Results, Experiments 1-2, opening paragraph.

confirmed.statement: S3: Participants were randomly assigned to the four between-subjects cells crossing Perplexity AI versus no LLM with a 10-cent bonus per correct prediction versus no bonus; other procedures matched Experiment 1.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 13, Materials and Methods, Experiment 3; p. 6, Results, Experiment 3, opening paragraph.

confirmed.statement: S4: Participants were randomly assigned to all four combinations of LLM versus no LLM in Stage 1 and Stage 2; the assigned tool was Google Bard, and the comparison used their own judgment with a search engine.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 13, Materials and Methods, Experiment 4.

confirmed.statement: S4: The randomized between-subjects arms include both AI-then-no-AI and no-AI-then-AI sequences, as well as AI in both stages and neither stage; condition order in the switching arms therefore follows randomized sequence assignment.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 13, Experiment 4, explicit random assignment to the Stage 1 by Stage 2 factorial; p. 7, Results, Experiment 4.

confirmed.statement: S1-S4: The document identifies Perplexity AI and Google Bard as LLMs producing suggestions from participants' own prompts; participants could retain or reject suggestions and add their own teams, supporting the generative_ai and open_chat coding.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Paradigm, final paragraph; p. 10, LLM output quality and hypothesis generation.

confirmed.statement: S1-S4: Assistance was used to generate participants' own submitted team lists; assignment did not merely change whose existing output participants evaluated.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 4-5, Paradigm; pp. 12-13, Materials and Methods, Experiments 1-4.

confirmed.statement: S1-S4: No-LLM conditions permitted search tools and did not explicitly prohibit LLMs; self-reported LLM users in those conditions were excluded after the task, as already acknowledged in the form.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 4-5, Paradigm, condition instructions and exclusion rule; p. 12, Experiment 1; p. 13, Experiments 2-4.

confirmed.statement: S3: The ai_tool description matches the reported retention of 79.7% of LLM-suggested teams (SD 27.2%) and participant additions comprising 3.0% of submitted hypotheses (SD 11.8%).
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10, LLM output quality and hypothesis generation.

confirmed.statement: S4: Stage 2 displayed the participant's Stage 1 list, invited additional teams, and could be skipped; participants reported resources and search prompts separately for each stage.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 13, Materials and Methods, Experiment 4.

summary: The PDF explicitly supports randomized generative-AI assistance in S1-S4 and matches the form's tools and comparison arms. S4 randomly assigns the four AI-use sequences, so the assignment criterion holds.
